Customer to confirm forecasted TPS and P50 latency targets by 2026-06-20
action_items: Maya Patel: Send detailed pricing and SLA options for dedicated reserved capacity + APAC burst (due 2026-06-18)
Connor Lee: Draft pilot runbook for EU private deployment and required infra checklist (due 2026-06-22)
Sofia Chen: Share current infra VPC peering and KMS policy docs (due 2026-06-18)

meeting_header: Date: 2026-06-15 | Time: 14:00 UTC | Duration: 42 mins | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Lee (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Gateway), Jonas Meyer (CTO), Liam O'Neill (Procurement), Sofia Chen (Platform)
summary: Check-in focused on renewal timing, sizing for APAC burst and EU private pilot, security/contract questions, and next-step to run a short on-prem pilot. Customer leaning toward a 12-month extension with reserved capacity + burst; needs pricing and a pilot runbook.
topics: Contract term and pricing (12-month extension vs monthly commit)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Anika (Gateway): Hi, Anika here.
[00:06] Jonas (CTO): Jonas on for Gateway.
[00:07] Liam (Procurement): Liam here.
[00:09] Sofia (Platform): Sofia, ready.
[00:11] Connor (Redwood SE): Connor, hi all.
[00:12] Maya: Awesome. We're here to go over renewal and the capacity expansion you mentioned for APAC and EU pilot -- check expectations and next steps.
[00:25] Anika: Yeah, quick context. We're generally happy with latency but are seeing very seasonal spikes in APAC, especially evenings. We're looking at a reserve + burst model and also want to trial EU private for data residency. Timeline is, ideally, contract signed before end of Q3.
[00:42] Maya: Great. On the numbers you shared last week, you showed 350 TPS p95 during peak windows globally, is that still accurate?
[00:49] Anika: Peak is about that, but APAC peaks are short lived, say 10-20 minutes but they hit twice a day.
[00:56] Jonas: And we care about p50 of 80-120ms for simple prompt paths; p95 can be up to 500ms and that's okay.
[01:04] Connor: Understood. For burst we can do dedicated reserved baseline for US/EU and then APAC burst on hosted in-region to avoid cold starts — lower commit, still predictable SLO.
[01:18] Liam: For procurement, main question is pricing delta for burst. If you do reserved plus burst, what's the unit economics?
[01:24] Maya: We'll send a model. High level: reserved capacity buys lower per-token and predictable throughput; burst is on-demand at a higher rate but we have a capped burst package so you get cost predictability.
[01:36] Sofia: Question on EU private: how isolated is it? We need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:46] Connor: All supported. VPC peering + customer KMS (HSM integrations) and we can ship audit events to your S3/Syslog. There is some setup lead time — roughly 3 weeks to spin up the private control plane and validate.
[01:58] Sofia: 3 weeks is ok, but we also need the runbook for our infra team.
[02:03] Connor: We'll draft a runbook with infra checklist: VPC CIDR, route tables, NAT gateways, KMS policies, service account roles.
[02:11] Anika: Also, performance: we want you to validate quantization profiles — we've seen some quality drift in prior attempts. Can you run evals against our prompt set?
[02:21] Connor: Yes, we'll run a quick quantization assessment. We'll need a sample of prompt templates and a 7-day trace to understand sequence length distribution and cache hit rates.
[02:33] Jonas: How about SSO? We need SAML + SCIM for onboarding.
[02:37] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC via SSO groups. We'll include our security pack and SOC2 report in the packet.
[02:45] Liam: On contract length: we prefer 12 months to lock in pricing, but want a clause for traffic growth — an annual true-up rather than monthly overage shocks.
[02:55] Maya: Reasonable. We can offer a 12-month reserved commit with quarterly cadence for forecasting and a predictable overage band. We'll include terms in the pricing doc.
[03:05] Anika: Any known limitations on model variants in private? We use some of the open quant models and a few custom adapters.
[03:12] Connor: Private supports our verified model catalog and you can bring compatible variants. Custom adapters are trickier — we'd need to validate adapter binary compatibility. We'll flag that as item for the pilot.
[03:24] Maya: Practical next steps: we'll send pricing + SLA options, Connor will draft the EU private pilot runbook, and Sofia will share network/KMS docs.
[03:33] Sofia: Yes. Also, we want a short benchmark — maybe a 48-hour APAC soak with synthetic load before committing. Can we do that as part of pilot?
[03:41] Connor: Yes, we can provision a test window for soak and run the workload. We can also do multi-region routing tests to validate fallback policies.
[03:51] Jonas: About observability — we rely on token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency histograms. Do you retain traces long enough?
[03:58] Maya: Default retention is 30 days for detailed traces; add-on retention is available. We'll surface dashboards per-model/per-route and provide trace hooks.
[04:07] Liam: Procurement needs an estimate: if we do 12-month commit for 80% of forecast and burst for 20%, what is the high-level monthly commitment?
[04:15] Maya: We'll model that in the pricing. Give us a final forecast number and we'll produce a table with committed units, burst cap, and projected spend.
[04:24] Anika: We'll get that to you by Friday. Also, curious about fallback — if private region is down, can traffic route to hosted with data controls?
[04:33] Connor: Yes, safe fallback policy is supported — you can define that model variants in hosted are used but we can redact logs or restrict retention to meet data policies. There are config knobs around audit logging and PII masking.
[04:46] Maya: Okay, going to log the action items. Any questions on SLA?
[04:50] Jonas: SLA numbers look fine, just want clarification on scheduled maintenance windows and notification lead time.
[04:55] Maya: Standard maintenance window is 4 hours weekly for non-critical infra; for Private we can align windows with your change freeze. We'll include details.
[05:03] Sofia: From the infra side, we'll need a network test plan and sample CloudFormation/Terraform modules if available.
[05:09] Connor: We'll share Terraform snippets and the network checklist in the runbook.
[05:14] Liam: One procurement quirk: can we get a clause for price protection if GPU costs drop significantly?
[05:20] Maya: We can discuss an adjustment clause; typical approach is look-back pricing or a midpoint renegotiation at renewal. We'll put options in the doc.
[05:29] Anika: Perfect. I'm keen to start the EU pilot; if runbook looks good we can aim to flip the PO by mid-July.
[05:36] Maya: Great — goal: pricing out next week, runbook draft within 7 days, pilot kickoff week of 2026-06-29.
[05:44] Jonas: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:47] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the packet.
[05:50] [Meeting ends]
